examples.text: „Die ersten Karawansereien entstanden im späten 10. Jahrhundert in den seldschukischen Fürstentümern Zentralasiens.“
„Aber die Karawanserei ist überfüllt, meine Damen, und die Dienstboten sind weggelaufen.“

„Fußmärsche, Verkleidungen, sengende Hitze, wenig Geld, Nächte in (man kann es nur ahnen) wanzenverseuchten Karawansereien, kaum genießbares Essen: als sollte die Reise die im Collegium erworbene Qualität seiner körperlichen Belastungsfähigkeit auf die Probe stellen.“
„Der Mann, von dem unsere Heldin an den Feuern der Karawansereien das Erzählen lernte und der ihr all seine Märchen schenkte, blieb in Großen und Ganzen unserer Phantasie überlassen.“

„Um die gesamte Karawanenroute von etwa eintausendvierhundert Kilometern bewältigen zu können, waren die Händler auf Stützpunkte, auf Karawansereien, angewiesen, um dort rasten und Verpflegung aufnehmen zu können.“

glosses: A roadside inn, usually having a central courtyard where caravans (see sense 3) can rest, providing accommodation for travellers along trade routes in Asia and North Africa.

examples.text: A dervise travelling through Tartary, being arrived at the town of Balk, went into the king's palace by mistake, as thinking it to be a public inn, or caravansary. […] It happened that the king himself passed through the gallery during this debate, and, smiling at the mistake of the dervise, asked him how he could possibly be so dull as not to distinguish a palace from a caravansary? […] 'Ah, Sir,' said the dervise, a house that changes its inhabitants so often, and receives such a perpetual succession of guests, is not a palace, but a caravansary.'
But not in sumptuous Caravansary / The adventurer idles there, / Nor satiates wonder with her pomp and wealth; […]

The "wakálah," as the caravanserai or khan is called in Egypt, combines the offices of hotel, lodging house, and store. It is at Cairo, as at Constantinople, a massive pile of buildings surrounding a quadrangular "hosh" or court-yard.
Think, in this batter'd Caravanserai / Whose Doorways are alternate Night and Day, / How Sultán after Sultán with his Pomp / Abode his Hour or two, and went his way.
Eight days later, after leaving the desert and riding through neatly tended villages and snow-capped mountain scenery, he arrived there, hiring himself a room in a caravanserai near the bazaar.

[page 80] Research over the last thirty-five years suggests that further research is likely to increase the number of known caravanserais in a good state of preservation. Unfortunately the majority of the caravanserais either had no founding inscription or it has since disappeared, and of the ones that do exist not all mention the type of building. […] [page 81] Caravanserais served caravans, but they also had a multitude of other functions. It is generally agreed that they continued the function of the ribats in Transoxania, and therefore it is taken for granted that they had military uses.

glosses: A place resembling a caravanserai (sense 1) as being a place for resting temporarily, or a meeting place (especially one that is busy, or where people of different cultures encounter each other).

examples.text: Conſider, I beſeech you, vvhat proviſion and accommodation, the Author of our being has prepared for us, that vve might not go on our vvay ſorrovving—hovv many caravanſera's of reſt—vvhat povvers and faculties he has given us for taking it—vvhat apt objects he has placed in our vvay to entertain us; […]

They stopped at the most memorable places, and at last arrived at Rome, where a princess vacated her palace for their accommodation and so many louis-d'or a-month. Rome, once the mistress, is now the caravanseray of the world.

Casting my fortunes at Mrs. Thompson's, I soon became initiated into the etiquette and usage of that polite caravansary; and I now write of that era of two-pronged forks, and when "saveall" was the choicest dish, and the observances at the table not altogether Chesterfieldian.

When we got to Cromley, it was too early to go to the spike, and we walked several miles farther, to a plantation beside a meadow, where one could sit down. It was a regular caravanserai of tramps—one could tell it by the worn grass and the sodden newspaper and rusty cans that they had left behind.
Only in Paris, a cosmopolitan caravansary in itself, did Americans and other foreigners fall nicely into the picture and spoil nothing in the charm of the place.

glosses: Synonym of caravan (“a convoy of travellers, their cargo and vehicles, and pack animals”).

examples.text: There they go, our brothers who have been educated at public schools and universities, mounting those steps, passing in and out of those doors,[…]. It is a solemn sight always—a procession, like a caravanserai crossing a desert.

glosses: A hostelry, an inn; also (humorous), an (upscale) hotel.

examples.text: By the bye it is as well to mention, for the benefit of the inexperienced, that there are no Inns in Ireland; all are hotels, from the lowest road cabin to the splendid caravanserai, with all its appurtenances of luxury and ease.

Six anxious inquiries of marble-fronted-hotel clerks about rates; and twice when she angrily made it plain she couldn't afford it, and quit the caravanserai where Andy and Mahala and Mrs Boyle were to loll in kitchenette-bedizened splendor and hunted up a smaller hotel that looked like a private house with obesity.

glosses: Vaste hôtellerie, dans le Proche-Orient, où logent les caravanes, les voyageurs et les bêtes de somme.

examples.text: Quoique l’auberge où nous étions logés ne fût pas de nature à nous donner une flatteuse idée des caravansérails orientaux, nous avions pu y trouver une chambre isolée et y recevoir des visites.

Vite au grand caravansérail. Là séjournent les caravanes venues de tous les points du continent asiatique. En voici une qui arrive, composée de marchands arméniens. En voilà une qui part, formée des trafiquants de la Perse et du Turkestan russe.
Le « Sunbeam Palace » n'en souffrait toutefois pas plus que les autres grands caravansérails du monde, quand une véritable épidémie de vols s'abattit sur lui.

Hors de la ville, un caravansérail à l’ombre des dattiers. Une muraille rectangulaire, des tourelles de surveillance, une cour extérieure pour les bêtes et les marchandises, une cour intérieure bordée de chambrettes.

Le jour commence à faiblir ; le ciel se fissure de rose ; une légère brise marine rafraîchit le caravansérail, on a ouvert les portes en grand pour laisser entrer l'air qui parcourt à présent les arcades et agite tendrement les feuilles du figuier.

glosses: Lieu très fréquenté et animé par des personnes de diverses provenances.

examples.text: Nous voici de retour à Bastogne, dans une ville enfiévrée, où deux milles chauffeurs, milles voitures et cinq mille personne forment un vrai caravansérail.
